scan.lane: Lane 1 — France, hospitality job boards (national specialists, generalists, seasonal/alpine, and extras marketplaces), read 15 September 2026

players.name: L'Hôtellerie Restauration — Emploi
players.legal_structure: Job board attached to the sector's own trade newspaper (print + web)
players.model: Pay-per-listing plus an unlimited monthly subscription; CV database included
players.price: Annonce Plus 85 € HT, 30-day run, company page, CV database access. Forfait Mensuel 205 € HT/month for 1–5 establishments, unlimited postings, no commitment. Internship/apprenticeship listings free for 90 days. Read 2026-09-15.
players.free_for_workers: Yes — CV deposit, alerts and applications carry no candidate fee
players.curated: No. Anyone in the trade buys a listing; no screening of the employer, no removal for churn.
players.size_signal: 2 944 live offers and 8 685 active CVs on the day read; 532K monthly visits and 2.5M page views (ACPM 2025 average), 44K newsletter subscribers, 220K social followers.
players.source_quote: "2944 offres d'emploi" / "8685 CV Actifs" / "532K visites mensuelles site internet (moyenne ACPM 2025)"
players.weakness: It is a media property monetising its audience. Every listing looks identical, the establishment's reputation is invisible, and the free apprenticeship slot means the youngest candidates see the least-filtered end of the inventory.

players.name: HotelRestauJob
players.legal_structure: Job board with an add-on sourcing service (CV hunting done by their consultant)
players.model: Pay-per-listing, with a premium tier that bundles multi-distribution and sourced CVs
players.price: Classic 95 € for one standard listing. Pack of 5 at 415 € (from 475 €). Premium 345 € including sourcing and 60-day multi-distribution to France Travail, Google Jobs, Talent.com, Jobijoba, Adzuna, Jooble, LinkedIn. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No. Nothing on the pricing page conditions publication on the employer's practices.
players.size_signal: No audience or offer count published on its own pages. Premium promises "au moins 3 CVs sourcés" per listing, which reads as a small pool worked by hand.
players.source_quote: "Pour chaque annonce au moins 3 CVs sourcés sont proposés"
players.weakness: Sells reach it does not own — the premium tier is mostly re-posting to Indeed-class aggregators. No proprietary audience to defend.

players.name: Emploi CHR (emploichr.net)
players.legal_structure: Job board, SaaS-style subscription
players.model: Freemium: one free 15-day listing, then monthly unlimited posting, CV-database credits and employer-brand pages sold separately
players.price: Free: 1 listing, 15 days, once. Pack Annuel 59 €/month on 12 months, unlimited listings. Pack Liberté 79 €/month, no commitment. CVthèque 19 €/month (50 credits) or 49 €/month (250 credits). Marque employeur 29 €/month per establishment on 12 months, 39 €/month flexible. Mise en avant 79 € one-off, social reshare 19 € one-off. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No.
players.size_signal: Its own homepage counters render as "+0" for both offers and talent profiles — the platform is either very small or half-built.
players.source_quote: "59 €" per month, 12-month commitment, unlimited postings
players.weakness: The cleanest price list in the sector and apparently the least inventory behind it. Shows the price band a new entrant can charge — and that price alone wins nothing.

players.name: JobStaffHotel
players.legal_structure: Job board
players.model: Credit packs of listings plus unlimited subscriptions
players.price: 1 offer 17,60 €; 5 offers 78,77 € (15,75 € each); 10 offers 136,59 € (13,66 € each); unlimited month 165,92 €; unlimited year 932,69 € (≈78 €/month). Listings run 2 months and are pushed to Facebook, LinkedIn and Indeed. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No.
players.size_signal: No offer or CV counts published.
players.source_quote: 1 offre 17,60 € — diffusion 2 mois + Facebook, LinkedIn, Indeed
players.weakness: Prices at the floor of the market, which is what a board does when it has no audience of its own to sell.

players.name: HCR Emploi (UMIH × Troops)
players.legal_structure: Recruitment plus HR platform launched by the sector's main employers' union (UMIH) with Troops — it also generates the CDI/CDD/seasonal contract and the payslip, so it sits between a job board and a payroll tool
players.model: Employer subscription, tier named "Essential"
players.price: NOT READ — hcr-emploi.fr returned HTTP 403 to fetching, and UMIH's own launch release publishes no figure. Do not assume a price here.
players.free_for_workers: Not confirmed from the site itself
players.curated: Vets the CANDIDATE, not the employer: candidates submit CV and administrative documents which are verified before the application is validated. The employer side is unscreened.
players.size_signal: UMIH's own release claimed 10 000 qualified candidates and as many companies at launch (May 2021); no current figure published.
players.source_quote: "La plateforme a déjà 10'000 candidats qualifiés inscrits et autant d'entreprises réparties partout en France"
players.weakness: Owned by the employers' union. Structurally it cannot drop a member establishment for churning staff — its shareholders are the establishments. That is exactly the position a curated board is not in.

players.name: HospoJobs (by Holybelly)
players.legal_structure: Job board run by an operating restaurant group (Holybelly, Paris) as a community project, built on the JobBoardFire platform
players.model: Hand-picked listings; no paid tier visible
players.price: No price stated anywhere on the pages of its own site I could open. Écotable's restaurant blog describes it as 100% free and says Nicolas Alary himself filters which offers go live — that is a third-party account, not hospo.jobs's own words. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: YES — the only French hospitality board that says on its own front page that offers are selected by hand: "Jobs dans la restauration triés à la main depuis 2016". Listings carry salary, hours and benefits, and candidates are put in touch with a named contact at the restaurant.
players.size_signal: "164 jobs postés depuis le 1er avril 2026" — roughly 35 listings a month, Paris-weighted.
players.source_quote: "Jobs dans la restauration triés à la main depuis 2016"
players.weakness: This is the plan, already built — but free, Paris-only, ten years old and still at ~35 listings a month, with the curation depending on one restaurateur's personal judgement and reputation. It proves the demand exists and that nobody has found the money in it.

players.name: Ohmyseason
players.legal_structure: Seasonal job marketplace with a paid human sourcing arm; not an interim agency — the employer signs the contract directly
players.model: Freemium listings (free Starter tier), paid subscription tiers on quote, plus per-placement sourcing
players.price: Starter free: 1 listing, limited applications, no CV database. Essentiel / Avancé / Custom carry NO published euro figure — "Contactez-nous". Sourcing is sold as "un tarif fixe par profil placé" with the amount withheld. A 5% commission on gross salary appears in search snippets attributed to an archived /old/tarifs page; I could not read that figure on the live page and am NOT asserting it. Read 2026-09-15.
players.free_for_workers: Yes — "La consultation des annonces, la création de votre profil et l'envoi de vos candidatures sont 100 % gratuits"
players.curated: Half. It vets the LISTING, not the house: every posting is verified with the establishment before publication for salary, housing, meals, schedules and working conditions, and over 80% of offers include accommodation. It does not judge the employer, and there is no mechanism for dropping one that churns staff.
players.size_signal: 450+ recruiting establishments, 300 000+ seasonal workers in the community, 50 000+ active candidates, 140 000+ profiles in the sourcing pool, 10 000+ WhatsApp alert subscribers, 4.8/5 on 40+ Google reviews.
players.source_quote: "100% Annonces vérifiées & claires"
players.weakness: The closest competitor and already inside Megève — it ran alongside the station's winter 2025-26 recruitment campaign. But it verifies a text, not a workplace, and it has no reason to remove a paying establishment. Its published price is zero to enter, which makes 'pay to be listed' a hard first ask in its territory.

players.name: Seasona
players.legal_structure: Seasonal job marketplace, mobile-first
players.model: Employer subscription (monthly, annual, or lifetime); bilateral post-mission ratings
players.price: Pro 29,99 €/month no commitment; 299,99 €/year; 899,99 € lifetime one-off. All tiers: centralised postings, applications, messaging, post-mission ratings. Read 2026-09-15.
players.free_for_workers: Yes — "Seasona est gratuit pour les saisonniers, pour toujours"
players.curated: No pre-vetting. It has bilateral post-mission ratings, so reputation accrues after the fact — a worker can see how an employer was rated, but nothing stops a badly-rated house from continuing to post.
players.size_signal: No offer, employer or user counts published. The lifetime tier at 899,99 € is what a very early platform sells to raise cash.
players.source_quote: "Seasona est gratuit pour les saisonniers, pour toujours"
players.weakness: New and thin, but it already owns the employer-subscription shape at roughly the price point a curated alpine board would charge. Watch it.

players.name: Tasaison
players.legal_structure: Seasonal job board with algorithmic matching
players.model: Pay per listing, no subscription
players.price: 8 € per listing published — "Seulement 8€ par annonce publiée", no subscription, no hidden fee. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No.
players.size_signal: No user or offer counts published.
players.source_quote: "Seulement 8€ par annonce publiée"
players.weakness: Sets the floor of the seasonal market at 8 € a listing. Any paid model has to explain why it is worth ten to thirty times that.

players.name: Mon Job À La Montagne
players.legal_structure: Job board attached to a physical recruitment forum, run by CNPC Sport (Centre National Professionnel pour la Commercialisation des articles de sports et de loisirs)
players.model: Free both sides; the site is the shop window for the annual Job Montagnes Alpes forum in Grenoble
players.who_pays: unclear — neither side pays for the site; the forum and CNPC's own training contracts carry the economics
players.price: Free. "La dépose des offres d'emploi est gratuite pour tous les recruteurs et illimitée". Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No vetting or approval process described; recruiters self-register and post.
players.size_signal: The associated forum, running since 2002, "offre chaque année plus de 2000 emplois saisonniers à pourvoir"; the website itself showed roughly 15 live listings when read.
players.source_quote: "La dépose des offres d'emploi est gratuite pour tous les recruteurs et illimitée"
players.weakness: 2 000 jobs a year exist at the forum and about fifteen on the website. The incumbent in alpine seasonal recruitment is an event, not a platform — which is the opening, and also the thing to beat.

players.name: Megève Jobs
players.legal_structure: Virtual recruitment forum run by Megève Tourisme (the destination's tourist office), hosted on the American vFairs event platform — not a job board
players.model: Time-boxed online hiring event: candidate registers, browses offers, books live chat interviews with recruiters
players.who_pays: unclear — free for candidates; no employer price published anywhere on the site
players.price: Free for candidates: "L'inscription et la participation à Megève Jobs sont entièrement gratuites pour les candidats". Employer cost NOT PUBLISHED on the site. Next edition 1, 2, 5 and 6 October 2026. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: De facto, on the wrong axis. Participation is by membership of the Megève destination, not by working conditions — Four Seasons Megève, Novotel Megève, Les Fermes de Marie, ESF Megève, Oxygène Ski all appear. No filtering on how staff are treated.
players.size_signal: Winter 2025-26 edition: about forty employers and nearly 500 offers, opened beyond hotels to restaurants, retail, real estate, activity providers and the mairie. First edition drew 1 300 registrations and nearly 1 800 applications.
players.source_quote: "Rendez-vous les 1, 2, 5 et 6 octobre 2026"
players.weakness: This is the direct incumbent in his first market and the hardest fact in this report: Megève's own tourist office already runs a free, branded, curated-by-membership hiring event with the town's best houses in it. A paid curated board in Megève competes with the mairie's own free product — or partners with it.

players.name: Job Tourisme
players.legal_structure: Job board covering tourism generally, with a mountain section
players.model: Employer accounts; "Devenir client"
players.price: No price published on the site; a client form gates it. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No.
players.size_signal: Employer profiles show volume — Club Med 61 offers, Intersport France 388 — but no site-wide total.
players.source_quote: Describes itself as the employment platform for tourism professionals
players.weakness: Sells to chains, not to the independent alpine hotel. Wrong customer for the commis-for-the-season problem.

players.name: Likeo
players.legal_structure: Was a hospitality recruitment app (founded 2019, Lyon) built on mutual employer/employee ratings; the domain now serves a general work-and-business content site
players.model: Unclear today
players.price: No price published. IMPORTANT: likeo.fr today renders as a blog — "votre espace d'inspiration et de ressources dédié à l'univers du travail et de l'entrepreneuriat" — and its /recruteurs page is an editorial round-up of recruitment agencies, not a product page. The employer-rating product is described only by third-party press and SEO pages. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: This was the one that tried the differentiator: cross-rating of employers by workers, with working-condition transparency visible before applying. I could not confirm the feature is live on the company's own site.
players.size_signal: Press claims 50 000 registered professionals and 3 240 offers; none of it verifiable on likeo.fr itself today.
players.source_quote: "Bienvenue sur le blog Likeo, votre espace d'inspiration et de ressources pratiques dédié à l'univers du travail et de l'entrepreneuriat"
players.weakness: Treat as a cautionary tale, not a competitor. The nearest thing France had to employer-condition transparency in hospitality appears to have turned into an SEO content site. Worth ten minutes on societe.com before building the same feature.

players.name: FoodJober
players.legal_structure: Job board, CHR-specialised
players.model: Free listings with a "FoodJober+" paid tier
players.price: Listings free — "Publiez vos offres gratuitement". A FoodJober+ tier is referenced in the footer with no price attached. Read 2026-09-15.
players.free_for_workers: Yes — "gratuit à 100 % : profil, CV, recherche d'offres et candidatures illimitées, sans aucune option payante"
players.curated: No.
players.size_signal: No counts published; shows Beefbar and Abbaye de Talloires as reference clients — note the second is Haute-Savoie.
players.source_quote: "gratuit à 100 % : profil, CV, recherche d'offres et candidatures illimitées"
players.weakness: Free-to-post, which trains establishments to expect zero. Already has a Haute-Savoie name on its wall.

players.name: Brigad
players.legal_structure: Marketplace of independent contractors (auto-entrepreneurs) — NOT an interim agency and NOT a job board. The talent invoices the establishment; Brigad handles invoicing, contracts and AXA professional liability cover. Carries known URSSAF requalification exposure for the establishments using it.
players.model: Percentage service fee on each mission
players.who_pays: both — the establishment pays a fee and the talent pays one
players.price: "Vous payez des frais des services sur chaque mission effectuée par un talent : 10% HT du total facturé par le talent." Note: third-party write-ups quote 25% all-in across both sides; the 10% HT is what Brigad's own page states for the business. Read 2026-09-15.
players.free_for_workers: No — talents also pay a service fee
players.curated: No condition-based vetting of establishments. It verifies the talent.
players.size_signal: Established player across France, UK and Spain; no figure taken from its own page here.
players.source_quote: "10% HT du total facturé par le talent"
players.weakness: Different business entirely — it sells shifts, not careers, and it is the thing a young commis should probably not start on. But it is where a Megève restaurant turns at 6pm on a Friday, and it is the revenue benchmark: 10% of every hour beats any listing fee.

players.name: Extracadabra
players.legal_structure: Multi-model at once: job board (CDI/CDD), licensed interim agency, and marketplace of auto-entrepreneurs. The legal wrapper changes per mission type.
players.model: Establishment sets the hourly rate for a mission; Extracadabra monetises the interim and placement legs
players.price: No euro figure or commission published on its own site. States it takes no commission on auto-entrepreneur invoices; the establishment "définit le tarif horaire selon les qualifications requises". Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No vetting of establishments on conditions.
players.size_signal: 10 000+ companies; 800–1 300 offers live per day; Paris, Lyon and Lille.
players.source_quote: 10 000+ companies use the platform; 800–1 300 daily offers
players.weakness: Urban. Paris/Lyon/Lille — it is not solving Megève in December.

players.name: Alloextra
players.legal_structure: CHR job board oriented to extras; direct-connection platform, not an interim agency and not on anyone's payroll
players.model: First listing free, then paid; CV-database access sold as 5-day, 30-day or 1-year subscriptions
players.price: "1ère annonce gratuite", subsequent listings paid; CVthèque subscriptions in 5-day / 30-day / 1-year terms. No euro figures published on the pages I could open (its /tarifs path returns a 404). Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No.
players.size_signal: Publishes no counts; runs a large SEO content operation around hospitality recruitment.
players.source_quote: "1ère annonce gratuite"
players.weakness: Monetises content and CV access rather than listings. Its own blog ranks for "best hospitality job sites" — it competes for attention more than for employers.

players.name: Hosco
players.country: Spain (Barcelona), with Geneva and Dubai offices; serves France
players.legal_structure: International hospitality job board and talent network, plugged into hospitality schools whose career sites it powers
players.model: Free company account and free branded career page; paid visibility and volume tiers on quote
players.price: Free company account and free career page — "Setting up and maintaining this page doesn't require any kind of commitment and is free of charge". Paid tiers are quote-only; a third-party review puts specialised hospitality boards in the $249–$375 per-posting band, which I am NOT attributing to Hosco. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No condition-based vetting. Its selectivity is on the candidate side, through the school network.
players.size_signal: 2M+ professionals, 1.7M+ hospitality-interested profiles; job posts auto-publish to partner schools' career sites.
players.source_quote: "2M+ professionals" / "1.7M+ hospitality-interested profiles"
players.weakness: Palace-and-chain oriented, English-first. But note the mechanism worth stealing: it reaches young people entering the trade through their schools, not through job search.

players.name: HelloWork
players.legal_structure: Generalist job board group
players.model: Free tier then flat monthly subscription banded by company size
players.price: Free: 2 job postings. 1–10 employees: 99 €/month, no commitment. 11–50 employees: 299 €/month, no commitment. 50+: annual quote. All paid tiers include CV database and the Buddi ATS. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No.
players.size_signal: 8M+ candidate profiles in the CV database; 33 650+ restaurant-sector offers listed at the end of August 2026.
players.source_quote: 99 €/month for 1–10 employees, no commitment, unlimited postings
players.weakness: The honest price ceiling. A Megève hotel with eight staff pays 99 €/month for the whole French labour market. A one-region curated board must be worth that against a national audience.

players.name: Indeed France
players.legal_structure: Generalist aggregator and job board
players.model: Free postings subject to quality criteria; sponsored postings auction-priced per click or started application
players.price: Free postings available "sous réserve des conditions générales, des critères de qualité et des limites d'utilisation". Sponsored: no fixed rate — priced by market competition, billed on the 1st of the month or when spend hits 500 €, whichever comes first. No commitment. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No — the closest thing is an automated quality filter on the posting, not on the employer.
players.size_signal: Carries the actual seasonal volume: 300+ seasonal postings for Chamonix-Mont-Blanc, 400+ for Haute-Savoie, 495 in the Megève area on the dates read.
players.source_quote: "Vous ne payez que lorsque les candidats cliquent sur vos annonces sponsorisées"
players.weakness: This is what the Megève hotel actually uses, and it is free to start. Not a quality competitor — a gravity well. Any new board's real fight is for the employer's second, deliberate listing, not their first desperate one.

players.name: Espaces Saisonniers de Chamonix et Megève / Maison de l'Emploi
players.legal_structure: Public-service structures — welcome, information and support points for seasonal workers, referenced by the Préfecture de Haute-Savoie, operated with the local Maison de l'Emploi
players.model: Free public service on both sides: job-offer distribution and recruitment support for employers, and employment, training, health, housing, labour-law and transport help for seasonal workers
players.price: Free. NOT READ DIRECTLY: saison-mont-blanc.fr returned HTTP 403 and maison-emploi.com failed TLS handshake. The description above comes from the Préfecture's own page, which names saison-mont-blanc.fr as the reference site.
players.curated: No selection on conditions — but note these are the bodies that hear the complaints when a seasonal job goes wrong, which makes them the natural source of evidence about which houses churn.
players.size_signal: Not published; Megève and Chamonix each have one, coordinated from Bonneville.
players.source_quote: "lieux d'accueil, d'information et de services" for seasonal workers
players.weakness: Not a competitor. A distribution channel and a data source — the Espace Saisonnier already sits between the young commis and the bad employer, for free, and knows which houses to warn about.

players.name: Meteojob
players.legal_structure: Generalist job board with matching technology
players.model: Quote-only; no free posting
players.price: NO PRICE PUBLISHED — the recruiter page gates pricing behind a contact form and a phone number. Do not assume a figure. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No.
players.size_signal: 14.5M registered users, 5.7M active CVs, 1.4M applications/month, and 1.51M candidates registered in the hospitality/restaurant category.
players.source_quote: 1.51M candidates in the Hôtellerie/Restauration category
players.weakness: Enterprise sales motion, opaque pricing. Irrelevant to a twelve-cover restaurant in Megève.

players.name: Cafe-Hotel-Restaurant.com (emploi)
players.legal_structure: Job board attached to a CHR trade portal
players.model: Free posting
players.price: Free — "Publier une annonce gratuitement". Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: No.
players.size_signal: Five live job listings on the page when read.
players.source_quote: "Publier une annonce gratuitement"
players.weakness: Five listings. Included only to show what free-and-unmoderated decays into — the graveyard end of this market is crowded.

scan.gap: The curation he is describing does not exist as a business anywhere in France. It exists twice as a fragment. HospoJobs (hospo.jobs, run by the Holybelly restaurant in Paris) does the exact editorial act — "Jobs dans la restauration triés à la main depuis 2016", offers hand-picked by the founder, salary and hours stated up front — and takes no money for it, after ten years, at roughly 35 listings a month, in Paris only. Ohmyseason does the exact commercial act — employers pay, candidates never do, 450+ establishments, 300 000 seasonal workers — and verifies the LISTING (salary, housing, meals, schedules, 80%+ with accommodation) rather than the HOUSE. Nobody in this lane operates the second half of his idea: quietly dropping an establishment that churns staff. The reason is structural and it is the whole thesis. Every incumbent is paid per listing or per month — an establishment that reposts the same commis job four times a season is its best customer, so removing churners destroys its own revenue line. HCR Emploi cannot do it at all: it is owned by UMIH, the employers' union, and the churners are its members. The one French platform that tried worker-side employer transparency, Likeo (Lyon, 2019, mutual employer/employee ratings), now serves a generic business blog at likeo.fr with no product visible — check that before rebuilding the same feature. Two hard obstacles specific to the first market. First, price: the sector clears at 8 € a listing (Tasaison), 17,60 € (JobStaffHotel), 85 € (L'Hôtellerie Restauration), or 59–99 €/month unlimited (Emploi CHR, HelloWork) — and the seasonal-alpine boards are free on the employer side (Mon Job À La Montagne: "gratuite pour tous les recruteurs et illimitée"; Ohmyseason Starter; FoodJober). Second, and harder: Megève's own tourist office already runs the curated hiring venue. Megève Jobs, a free virtual forum on vFairs, ~40 employers and ~500 offers for winter, first edition 1 300 registrations and 1 800 applications, next edition 1, 2, 5 and 6 October 2026 — with Four Seasons, Les Fermes de Marie, Novotel and ESF inside it. It curates by destination membership, never by conditions, and it is free. The gap is therefore narrow and real: paid, permanent, condition-curated, with exclusion as the product — and the thing to check first is whether Megève Tourisme is a partner or the competitor.
scan.bottom_line: What a Megève or Haute-Savoie house actually uses today to find a commis for the season, in order: Indeed (free to start, 495 seasonal listings in the Megève area, 400+ across Haute-Savoie — this is the gravity well), the mairie's small-ads page, Megève Tourisme's own free Megève Jobs virtual forum each autumn, Ohmyseason (already the station's recruitment partner for the winter 2025-26 campaign), and word of mouth through the Espace Saisonnier at Megève or Chamonix. Almost none of that is a paid hospitality job board. The national specialists — L'Hôtellerie Restauration at 85 € a listing on 532K monthly visits, HotelRestauJob at 95 €, Emploi CHR at 59 €/month — sell to establishments that have already decided to advertise; the alpine seasonal layer is free. Nobody filters employers on how they treat people. HospoJobs does it by hand and charges nothing; Ohmyseason charges and verifies only the text of the ad. The differentiator survives the scan intact, but the pricing does not survive it easily: he is proposing to charge in a market where the alpine incumbents are free and the town hall is one of them. Three things to settle before building anything: whether the exclusion rule is enforceable on evidence he can actually obtain (the Espaces Saisonniers hear the complaints and are publicly funded — talk to them); whether Megève Tourisme wants a year-round partner or will treat him as a rival to Megève Jobs; and what happened to Likeo, because it is the only French company that tried to make employer conditions visible in this sector and its website is now a content farm.

scan.lane: Lane 2 — France: extras, shift marketplaces and HCR job boards. Eleven live sites opened and priced on 15 September 2026. Two groups emerged and they are not the same business: (A) transaction platforms that place a worker and take a cut of the shift — Brigad, Extracadabra, StaffMe, Side, Staffmatch; (B) paid-listing job boards where the establishment buys visibility and nothing flows through the operator — Restaff, FoodJober, Seasona, L'Hôtellerie Restauration, HotelRestauJob, AlloExtra. The planned site is group B. The legally interesting fights are all in group A, and none of them reach group B.

players.name: Brigad
players.model: Marketplace of independent professionals (micro-entrepreneurs) taking single shifts in hôtellerie-restauration and healthcare. Brigad handles the contract, the invoice and the URSSAF declaration, and insures the worker through Axa. Both sides are charged.
players.legal_structure: Marketplace of auto-entrepreneurs, explicitly NOT an interim agency. Its terms describe it as an 'opérateur de plateforme en ligne' assuming no responsibility for the contractual relationship. This was litigated: the temp agency Staffmatch sued to have Brigad's activity banned as evasion of interim regulation, and the Cour de cassation (chambre sociale, 12 November 2020, n°19-10.606) rejected Staffmatch — but in référé only, the provisional-and-urgent judge. Brigad's own blog post declares 'Brigad n'est pas une Entreprise de Travail Temporaire'. TendanceHôtellerie's rebuttal points out the merits have never been judged and that a separate criminal case, in which Staffmatch and the employers' union Prism'emploi joined as civil parties alleging concealment of salaried employment, was still open.
players.price: Establishment: 10% HT of the total invoiced by the talent, per completed mission (covers 24/7 support, automated invoicing and contracts, Axa liability cover, access to the vetted pool). Talent: 15% TTC per completed mission, 9.9% TTC for nursing missions. Fees have been split between the two sides since 15 November 2023. Read 15 September 2026 on brigad.co's own two fee pages.
players.free_for_workers: NO — this is the sharpest contrast with the planned site. The worker pays 15% TTC of every mission. On a 100 € shift the worker keeps 85 € before social contributions. French law forbids charging a job seeker for placement (Code du travail, art. L5321-3: no direct or indirect remuneration may be required from a job seeker for a placement service, punishable by six months and 3,750 €); Brigad's answer is that it is a platform, not a placement operator — which is precisely what the Staffmatch litigation is about.
players.curated: NO — and the terms say so structurally. Brigad's CGU carry a suspension article aimed at talents and no equivalent power over establishments. The feedback loop runs establishment→talent: establishments rate talents, and establishments are shown talents well rated by comparable houses. There is no route by which a house that churns staff loses access.
players.size_signal: Own homepage claims 12,000+ establishments and 23,000+ professionals. Raised a €33M Series B in February 2023 led by Balderton Capital (€22M) with Wendel, Serena and Square Capital (€6M) plus €5M debt. Stated 200,000 missions in 2022, targeting over a million in 2024.
players.source_quote: « 10% HT du total facturé par le talent » (establishments) and « 15% TTC de frais de service sur chaque mission » (talents)
players.weakness: The worker pays. That is the single fact the planned site can point at. Second: the requalification risk does not sit on Brigad, it sits on the restaurant that books the extra — the platform is the matcher, the client company is the one URSSAF audits. Third: no lever over bad employers at all.

players.name: Extracadabra
players.model: Matching platform for hôtellerie-restauration, événementiel and retail. Four employer products: Extra (short CDD), Intérim, Saisonnier, CDI. Publishing a mission request as an extra is free; the fee falls when a matched candidate actually turns up to work.
players.legal_structure: Mixed, and deliberately so. The CGU state Extracadabra acts 'exclusivement en qualité d'intermédiaire exerçant une activité de mise en relation' and as a mandataire d'encaissement (collection agent) for the independents — never a party to the contract. Interim is delivered through partner ETTs, to which Extracadabra remains 'strictement tiers à la relation de travail'. So: an intermediary for independents, an introducer for licensed temp agencies, and a paid job board for CDI. Its 2025 investor is Actual Ventures, the corporate fund of the interim group Actual — whose president praised the company's 'solid regulatory approach'.
players.price: Published in the CGU, read 15 September 2026: single CDI advert 95 € HT (held 10 days on the site and app); unlimited-advert subscription 235 € HT per month. Late cancellation of a mission costs the establishment 30% of the forecast hours, capped at 150 € HT. The per-mission matching commission for extras is NOT published anywhere on the site — the CGU say only that Extracadabra 'perçoit séparément et pour son propre compte la commission'. https://www.extracadabra.com/tarifs returns 404. A 2019 Journal du Net piece put the scale at 10 € for a one-day mission to ~400 € for contracts over six months; that number is second-hand and I could not confirm it on the company's own pages.
players.free_for_workers: Yes, no fee is charged to the candidate — but the CGU push the economic risk onto them: 'le risque économique lié à la défaillance éventuelle de l'Établissement client demeure entièrement à votre charge'. If the restaurant does not pay, that is the extra's problem.
players.curated: NO. Nothing on the site or in the terms vets, rates or excludes establishments on working conditions.
players.size_signal: €27M revenue in 2024, up from €2.5M pre-Covid. €15M financing from Actual Ventures announced 19 March 2025. Over 6,000 active candidates working with more than 3,000 companies in 2024. Founded 2015 by Frédéric Nardon and Rémi Boisson. Earlier rounds: €150k (2016), €1.2M (2018), €1.5M (2020).
players.source_quote: « 95 € HT par annonce » and « 235 euros HT par mois » for unlimited listings
players.weakness: Opaque per-mission pricing — an establishment cannot find out what an extra costs without signing up. And the CDI-advert price (95 € one-off, 235 €/month unlimited) is a direct price anchor for the planned site: it is what a French HCR employer already pays for a listing from the biggest specialist name.

players.name: StaffMe
players.country: France (owned by House of HR, Belgium)
players.model: Two products under one brand. StaffMe Freelance: a marketplace of auto-entrepreneurs, historically aimed at 18-30 year olds, which also helps them register as auto-entrepreneur. StaffMe Intérim: a licensed temp agency. Sectors served include Hôtellerie-Restauration and Événementiel.
players.legal_structure: Split — this is the most instructive structure in the lane. The Freelance side is a 'place de marché en ligne dédiée à la mise en relation de Travailleurs indépendants et des Entreprises'. The Interim side is a declared ETT: the CGU state 'StaffMe Solutions by NowJobs est une entreprise de travail temporaire' with Société Générale as financial guarantor under art. L1251-49 of the Code du travail. StaffMe therefore runs the risky model and the regulated model side by side, under separate legal entities.
players.price: Freelance: commission of 20% du Prix global, charged to the company (CGU, read 15 September 2026). Placement into permanent roles: 8-10% of annual gross salary. Interim: an undisclosed coefficient applied to the temp's cost, quoted case by case — no public rate. The help-centre article stating a minimum 18 € HT/hour of which the freelancer receives 14.40 € returned HTTP 403 to me, so I do not assert that figure as read.
players.free_for_workers: Nominally yes — the CGU say the service is 'à titre payant pour l'Entreprise et à titre gratuit pour le Travailleur indépendant'. Economically it is thinner than that: the 20% is taken out of the price the company posts, so the freelancer nets 80% of the advertised mission price.
players.curated: NO. StaffMe vets the worker (diploma, status, motivation, permit), not the employer.
players.size_signal: Own site claims 800,000+ candidate profiles and 12,000+ client companies. Founded 2016 by Amaury d'Everlange and Jean-Baptiste Achard; raised €500k in 2016; acquired by the Belgian group House of HR in September 2022 and paired with its NOWJOBS platform.
players.source_quote: « StaffMe Solutions by NowJobs est une entreprise de travail temporaire » — the interim arm; the freelance arm is a « place de marché en ligne »
players.weakness: It is the lane's cautionary tale on reputation. Basta! published an investigation on 5 September 2022 on StaffMe, Student Pop and Manners, arguing the model sells flexibility to young and often precarious workers while stripping the protections of salaried status; the lawyer Kévin Mention is quoted there saying it is no accident these platforms target the young. StaffMe was named alongside Monoprix in a prud'hommes case listed for late 2022. Syndicoop ran a companion piece titled on student precarity. A site aimed at young people entering the trade is competing for exactly this audience's trust.

players.name: Side
players.model: Fully online interim agency. Four products: Side Source (end-to-end interim recruitment), Side Flash (admin only, for candidates the client already found), Side Horizon (CDI placement), Side Saisons (seasonal).
players.legal_structure: Entreprise de travail temporaire — and it got there by retreating. Side spent its first three years as a marketplace of student auto-entrepreneurs, obtained ETT status in April 2019 and moved 100% of missions onto interim contracts by September 2019. Its own stated reasons were that freelancers and employees doing identical work on the same sites create requalification risk for the client company, and that a salarié is far better protected. Part of the Randstad group since May 2022.
players.price: Not published. Pricing is a coefficient applied to the interim's cost, quoted on request; no public rate card anywhere on side.co. Read 15 September 2026.
players.free_for_workers: Yes — the worker is a salaried intérimaire and pays nothing.
players.curated: NO.
players.size_signal: Own site claims 500,000 Siders, 10,000 clients, 160+ employees, access to 850 Randstad agencies for seasonal work. Raised over €10M pre-acquisition from investors including Xavier Niel, Jacques-Antoine Granjon and Martin Bouygues.
players.source_quote: « Side transforme l'univers du travail temporaire grâce à une plateforme d'intérim en ligne »
players.weakness: Not actually a competitor in his sector. The sectors listed on side.co/entreprises are Retail/Vente, Logistique, Tertiaire, Tourisme and Agriculture — hôtellerie-restauration is not among them. Side matters here as legal precedent, not as a rival: it is the company that tried the auto-entrepreneur model in France and voluntarily abandoned it.

players.name: Staffmatch
players.model: Interim agency with a digital front end, with a dedicated hôtellerie-restauration desk (chef de cuisine, commis, serveur, maître d'hôtel) and a collective-catering desk. Workers are salaried intérimaires with IFM and ICCP.
players.legal_structure: Declared ETT, registered with the DRIEETS under art. R.1251-1 of the Code du travail, financial guarantee provided by Atradius under art. L.1251-50.
players.price: Not published — no rate or coefficient anywhere on the sector pages. Read 15 September 2026.
players.curated: NO.
players.size_signal: Multi-agency national network; size not stated on the pages opened.
players.source_quote: « Agence d'intérim dans l'hôtellerie et la restauration »
players.weakness: Listed here because it is the litigant, not because it competes with a listings site. Staffmatch is the HCR temp agency that took Brigad to court in 2018 and lost in référé up to the Cour de cassation in 2020 — the whole French map of what a shift platform may and may not do was drawn by this fight. Its relevance to the plan is that it shows who reacts when someone appears to be doing placement without an interim licence.

players.name: Restaff
players.model: Subscription job board for hôtellerie-restauration with matching and direct messaging between establishment and candidate. Closest structural twin to the plan: employer subscribes, candidate is free, no money moves through the operator, no placement fee.
players.legal_structure: Job board / listings marketplace. Not an interim agency, not a marketplace of independents — no worker contract or payment flow at all.
players.price: Read 15 September 2026 on the subscription page. Basique 39 € HT/month (29 €/month quarterly = 87 € HT; 19 €/month annual = 228 € HT): 1 establishment, 1 advert/month, social-media sharing. Professionnel 59 € HT/month (39 € quarterly; 29 € annual = 348 € HT): up to 5 adverts/month plus redistribution to partners. Premium 99 € HT/month (69 € quarterly; 49 € annual = 588 € HT): up to 5 establishments, 5 adverts each. Single advert without subscription 9 € HT. Seven-day free trial, no card required.
players.curated: NO — it verifies that the recruiter exists, not that it is decent. Account validation is by SIRET check. That is the whole of the filtering.
players.size_signal: Not disclosed on the site.
players.source_quote: « vous pouvez essayez Restaff gratuitement pendant 7 jours, sans carte bancaire »
players.weakness: It is the price ceiling he has to live under: 19-49 € HT/month on annual billing for a national HCR board. And its only employer check is a company-registration lookup — which is exactly the space the curation idea occupies.

players.name: FoodJober
players.model: CHR job-matching site covering service, kitchen, plonge and management across CDI, CDD, extra and seasonal. Its distinguishing feature is that working-condition attributes — predictable hours, meals included, atmosphere — are fields in the advert itself, surfaced to candidates at a glance.
players.legal_structure: Job board. No worker contract, no payment flow, no placement fee.
players.price: Read 15 September 2026. Pay-per-advert: 9,99 € per advert, immediate visibility, no subscription. FoodJober+ 75 €/month: up to 5 active adverts per month, automatic repost, promoted placement on the platform, cancellable at any time. FoodJober Pro: on quote — sourcing, interviews, reference checks, shortlist. No free tier for employers. Card payment via Stripe.
players.free_for_workers: Yes, and stated flatly: profile, CV, search and unlimited applications, with no paid option for jobers at all.
players.curated: NO — and this is the nearest miss in the whole lane. FoodJober surfaces working conditions but takes them as the employer's own declaration. It does not verify them, does not rate the establishment afterwards, and has no mechanism for dropping a house that churns staff. Its own blog cites a 2026 France Travail study putting working conditions as the first accept-or-refuse criterion for 68% of CHR workers — so the demand is identified and unserved.
players.size_signal: Not disclosed. Content-heavy blog aimed at CHR employers; appears recent and small.
players.source_quote: « 75 € / mois » for FoodJober+ (up to 5 active adverts, repost, promoted placement); « 9,99 € / annonce » one-off
players.weakness: Self-declared conditions with no verification is a claim, not a guarantee. Any employer can tick 'horaires prévisibles'. The planned site's promise — the operator has judged the house and will drop it — is the thing FoodJober stops short of.

players.name: Seasona
players.model: Seasonal-work platform matching establishments with saisonniers, with ski-station landing pages (Les Deux Alpes among them). Employer publishes a mission, applications and messages are centralised, and the mission is closed with a rating.
players.legal_structure: Job board / listings marketplace. Employer subscribes; no employment or payment intermediation.
players.price: Read 15 September 2026. Mensuel 29,99 € per month, no commitment. Annuel 299,99 € per year. À vie 899,99 € one-off payment. All tiers include mission publication, centralised applications and messages, real-time exchange and post-mission ratings.
players.free_for_workers: Yes, and permanently: the site states Seasona is free for saisonniers, forever — profile, search, applications and messaging at no cost.
players.curated: NO, and the asymmetry is the point. The rating system runs one way: the employer closes the mission and rates the workers, to guide its next hires. Workers do not rate the house and the house is not filtered on conditions.
players.size_signal: Not disclosed. Station-level pages exist for Alpine resorts, so it is already present in the geography the plan starts in.
players.source_quote: « Seasona est gratuit pour les saisonniers, pour toujours » — and 29,99 €/month, 299,99 €/year, 899,99 € à vie for employers
players.weakness: This is the closest live thing to the plan and it is already in the Alps — the model (employer subscription, worker free forever, seasonal) is taken. What it does not do is judge the employer, and it actively does the opposite: it hands the establishment a scoring tool over the worker. A lifetime pass at 899,99 € also tells you the operator does not expect to earn trust-based renewals.

players.name: L'Hôtellerie Restauration (emploi)
players.model: The trade newspaper's job board — the sector incumbent. Employers buy an advert or a CV-database subscription; candidates browse and apply free.
players.legal_structure: Job board run by a trade publisher. No placement, no interim, no worker payment flow.
players.price: Read 15 September 2026 on the pack page. Forfait Internet classique 158 € HT: 30 days online plus immediate email push to registered candidates. CV-database add-on +119 € HT for 10 days. Standalone CV-database subscriptions: 10 days (1 user, 500 CVs) 277 €; 1 month (1 user, 1,500 CVs) 790 €; 3 months (1 user, unlimited) 2,120 €. Degressive packs: 5 adverts −8%, 10 adverts −12%. Adverts for trainees and apprentices are free.
players.curated: NO — volume board, no employer filter.
players.size_signal: Claims over 50,000 job offers posted per year; the reference title of the French HCR trade press.
players.source_quote: « 158 € HT » for a 30-day internet advert; CV database from « 277 € » for 10 days
players.weakness: It is the price and credibility benchmark an establishment compares against: 158 € HT buys 30 days on the sector's most-read title. A new regional site has to be either much cheaper or visibly different in kind — which is what curation would be.

players.name: HotelRestauJob
players.model: HCR job board with multidiffusion — adverts are pushed for 60 days to France Travail, Google Jobs, Talent.com, Jobijoba, Adzuna, Jooble, Alljobs and LinkedIn. A premium tier adds CV sourcing.
players.legal_structure: Job board, operated by Jeanbauche SAS.
players.price: Read 15 September 2026. Classic 95 € per advert, no sourcing, 60-day multidiffusion. Pack of 5 adverts 415 € (from 475 €). Premium 345 € per advert with CV sourcing, at least 3 CVs sourced, a dedicated recruitment adviser and 24/7 candidate tracking.
players.free_for_workers: Yes — candidates deposit a CV and apply at no cost.
players.curated: NO.
players.size_signal: Not disclosed.
players.source_quote: « 95 € » per advert classic; pack of five « 415 € »; premium with sourcing « 345 € »
players.weakness: Sells reach, not judgement — the product is distribution to eight aggregators. Nothing in it is about whether the job is any good.

players.name: AlloExtra
players.model: Job board for finding extras in hôtellerie-restauration; recruiter registers, posts adverts, candidates register free. Listings observed were Lyon and Villeurbanne.
players.legal_structure: Job board. No interim licence claimed, no worker payment flow.
players.price: First advert free for recruiters; no further prices published on the site. Candidate registration free. Read 15 September 2026 — I could not find a published rate card, so I am not stating one.
players.curated: NO — nothing about employer screening anywhere on the site.
players.size_signal: Small, regionally concentrated (Rhône). Also publishes a round-up of HCR job sites, which is how it surfaces in searches.
players.source_quote: « Inscrivez-vous en tant que recruteur pour publier vos annonces (1ère annonce gratuite) »
players.weakness: Proof that a small regional HCR board is viable to launch and hard to make visible — it is nearly invisible in search next to the national names, and it gives adverts away to get started.

scan.gap:
Nobody in France vets the employer. Every one of the eleven sites verifies the worker and merely confirms the employer exists. Restaff's entire employer check is a SIRET lookup. Brigad's terms are the cleanest proof: they carry a suspension article aimed at talents and no equivalent power over establishments, and the feedback loop runs establishment→talent, so a house that churns staff can never lose access. Seasona goes further in the wrong direction — the employer closes the mission and rates the workers, with no reverse. FoodJober is the only near miss: it puts working conditions into the advert as structured fields, but they are the employer's own declaration, unverified, with no post-hire rating and no exclusion mechanism. So the ground is genuinely open in two ways at once: verified conditions rather than declared ones, and the power to drop a house.

The pricing gap is the opposite — crowded and cheap. The paid-listing model is proven and already priced across the whole range: 9 € HT for a one-off advert on Restaff, 9,99 € on FoodJober, 95 € on HotelRestauJob, 158 € HT for 30 days on the sector's own trade title; subscriptions at 19-49 € HT/month on Restaff annual, 29,99 €/month on Seasona, 75 €/month on FoodJober+, 235 € HT/month unlimited on Extracadabra. There is no pricing innovation left to find. The only defensible premium is the curation itself.

The geographic gap is thin, not absent. Seasona already runs Alpine station pages at 29,99 €/month with workers free forever. Starting in one alpine region does not buy empty ground; it buys the ability to actually go and look at the houses, which a national board at 9,99 € an advert cannot do at any price.

The legal gap is the largest and the least contested. His model has no worker, no mission, no payment flow and no matching, so it touches none of the exposure that shaped this lane: no requalification risk, no need for an ETT licence and financial guarantee, no URSSAF audit trail. The one rule that does bind him he already satisfies — Code du travail art. L5321-3 forbids requiring any direct or indirect payment from a job seeker in return for a placement service, on pain of six months and 3,750 €. Charging candidates nothing is not a positioning choice in France; it is the law, and Brigad's 15% talent fee survives only on the argument that a platform is not a placement operator — the argument Staffmatch has been contesting since 2018.
scan.bottom_line:
The French field splits cleanly and he is on the safe side of the split. Brigad, Extracadabra, StaffMe, Side and Staffmatch move people and money and have spent a decade fighting over what that makes them: Staffmatch sued Brigad to have it declared an unlicensed temp agency and lost in référé at the Cour de cassation on 12 November 2020 (n°19-10.606), with the merits and a criminal case still untried; Side looked at the same question in 2019, abandoned its auto-entrepreneur marketplace and took out an ETT licence; StaffMe hedged by running a freelance marketplace and a licensed ETT side by side. A paid directory with no matching, no placement fee and no payment flow sits outside all of it.

Two facts are worth carrying into his positioning. First, Brigad charges the worker 15% TTC of every mission — the only platform in the lane that does — and French law forbids charging a job seeker for placement, which is exactly the fault line Staffmatch has been pushing on. "Candidates pay nothing, ever" is not a differentiator against a job board; against Brigad it is.

Second, curation is genuinely unoccupied and the terms of service prove it rather than merely suggesting it: Brigad's CGU can suspend a talent and cannot touch an establishment. FoodJober is the one to watch, because it has already decided working conditions belong in the advert — it just takes the employer's word for them. The distance between "the restaurant says the hours are predictable" and "I went and checked, and I drop houses that churn" is the entire product.

What the plan does not get is pricing room. Eleven sites opened, and a listing in French HCR costs between 9 € one-off and 158 € HT for 30 days, with subscriptions clustering at 19-75 €/month. He will be selling into a market that already knows what an advert is worth. The premium has to come from the curation being real and being seen to be real — which is also the hardest thing on the list to operate, and the only one nobody else is doing.

scan.lane: Lane 3 — International hospitality hiring platforms (outside France): who charges whom, and whether anyone curates employers on working conditions

players.name: Countertalk
players.model: Curated hospitality job board plus editorial/community. Does not list every job — employers are approved and every ad is manually vetted before publication.
players.legal_structure: Job board / media platform. Not an agency, no placement fee, no interim, no marketplace of self-employed workers.
players.price: Essential £95 + VAT (live 4 weeks); Featured £195 + VAT (4 weeks); Premium £295 + VAT (6 weeks). Read 15 Sep 2026 on their own pricing page, FAQ and Terms — all three agree. Payment is taken via Stripe only after the post is approved.
players.free_for_workers: Yes — candidates create an account, apply and get alerts at no cost. The platform charges employers exclusively.
players.curated: YES — this is the one that does exactly what is being planned. Terms: "All job posts and profiles are subject to our internal vetting process and must be manually approved before being published." They reserve the right to "refuse, edit, or permanently remove any job advertisement" that reflects "a poor or unsafe working culture", and to reject an ad where "The employer is found to be in breach of the Countertalk Employer Pledge at the point of review." Employer page: "We approve and verify every hospitality employer." Public claim: only the top 3% of hospitality jobs are posted.
players.size_signal: Founded 2018 by Rav Gill. ~100+ verified employers listed, 17 pages of employer listings as of 15 Sep 2026. Eight years in and still roughly a hundred houses — curation caps supply.
players.weakness: Small and geographically concentrated (London and the independent/artisanal scene). A curated board has few ads, and few ads means weak candidate pull — the structural trap of this model. The removal right for "poor or unsafe working culture" is a right, not a mechanism: it fires on review, not on churn data. Nothing measures whether a listed employer actually retains staff.
players.source_quote: "All job posts and profiles are subject to our internal vetting process and must be manually approved before being published." / "Every role listed on Countertalk has met our criteria around culture, clarity, fairness and values."

players.name: Fair Job Hotels e.V.
players.model: Paid employer certification with a job board attached. Hotels apply, are assessed on working conditions, and pay an annual membership. The job board itself is white-labelled from hotelcareer.de rather than built in-house.
players.legal_structure: Registered association (eingetragener Verein, e.V.), Hamburg, founded 2016. Not a job board company, not an agency. Members are the hotels; candidates are the beneficiaries.
players.price: Annual membership by headcount, read on their own Partnerhotel-werden page 15 Sep 2026: up to 20 employees €1,250/year; 21–50 employees €2,500/year; 51+ employees €3,750/year. Recurring, and independent of how much the hotel hires.
players.free_for_workers: Yes — candidates search and apply free; they also get free access to the FAIRmittler / FAIRtrauensteam, an independent counsellor and conflict-mediation service.
players.curated: YES, and harder than Countertalk. A four-stage "Aufnahmejourney" judged by an expert panel across five areas: company culture, development of young staff, health and wellbeing, appropriate pay, and HR impact measurement. Only hotels already well positioned are admitted — rejections are routine. The ten "FAIRsprechen" bind members, including: "Wir gewähren eine faire Bezahlung. Mindestlohn und die Einhaltung von Tarifverträgen sind obligatorisch" and "Wir realisieren faire Arbeitszeiten. Zeiterfassung und die gesetzlichen Anforderungen sind für uns verpflichtend." Members must display a poster in the staff area giving contact details for an independent mediator — an ongoing complaint channel from the workforce straight past the employer.
players.size_signal: 117 member hotels across DE/AT/CH, roughly 10,500 employees. Members average 4.18 on kununu against an industry average of 3.4. Admission rules were loosened in the last few years (two sponsor hotels no longer required) to admit unclassified houses.
players.weakness: It takes money from the establishments it certifies — the same conflict of interest the planned French site will carry. Its credibility rests entirely on being seen to reject applicants. It also has no independent board: the jobs live on hotelcareer.de, so it never owns the candidate relationship. Hotels only, no restaurants.
players.source_quote: Jahresbeitrag: "bis 20 Mitarbeitende 1.250 € / Jahr", "21–50 Mitarbeitende 2.500 €", "ab 51 Mitarbeitende 3.750 €" — and "Wir gewähren eine faire Bezahlung. Mindestlohn und die Einhaltung von Tarifverträgen sind obligatorisch."

players.name: HOTELCAREER / Gastrojobs (with the "Fair Workplace" seal)
players.model: Mainstream pay-to-post hospitality job board, the German market leader, owned by Stepstone. It has bolted a working-conditions seal onto an ordinary board.
players.legal_structure: Job board. Operated by The Stepstone Group Deutschland GmbH (YOURCAREERGROUP).
players.price: Official price list (Stand 1/2025, read 15 Sep 2026): 1 position for 1 month €319; 3 positions 1 month €379; 3 positions 12 months €2.039; 40 positions 12 months €5.349 — all excl. VAT, per establishment, per destination. Premium extras: Top Listing €199/week, Premium Job €199/week, Jobfinder e-mail €269/day, Premium company profile €749 for 6 months or €1.289 for 12 months. Explicitly not available to temp agencies or recruiters.
players.curated: PARTIALLY — and this is the instructive near-miss. The "Fair Workplace" seal grades employers Bronze / Silber / Gold on working conditions. Bronze requires "Zahlung von Mindestlohn / Einhaltung von Tarifabschlüssen", "Zeiterfassung und die Einhaltung der gesetzlichen Arbeitszeit", and openness to all applicants regardless of origin, religion or sex. Silber adds a pension or 13th-month-type payments, plus parking or transport access; Gold adds flexible models, development, wellbeing and commuting support. BUT the seal is a badge on a pay-to-post board, not a gate — an employer without a seal still buys an ad and still appears. And the criteria read as declared benefit checkboxes; nothing on the page states who audits them.
players.size_signal: Germany's dominant hospitality board, Stepstone-owned, DE/AT/CH coverage. It is also the board Fair Job Hotels rents its job listings from.
players.weakness: A seal on a board that takes anyone's money is a marketing feature, not curation. Bronze is barely more than obeying the law — paying minimum wage and recording hours. Proves the demand for the signal without proving the model.
players.source_quote: Bronze criteria: "Zahlung von Mindestlohn / Einhaltung von Tarifabschlüssen" and "Zeiterfassung und die Einhaltung der gesetzlichen Arbeitszeit". Price list: "1 Monat 319 €" for one position, "Stand 1/2025".

players.name: Hosco
players.country: Switzerland (Geneva), with Barcelona and Dubai; global reach
players.model: Global hospitality careers network — job board plus candidate profiles, a school network and a learning arm. Freemium for employers: free company profile and free branded career page, paid credits and premium for reach and database access.
players.legal_structure: Job board / professional network. Also sells consultant-led recruitment services for mass hiring, which shades into agency work.
players.price: Not published. Their FAQ confirms the free tier — "There is no charge to become visible on the Hosco network with a company profile" — and that Credits and Premium are bought to contact candidates and post jobs, but no figure appears anywhere on their own site. Demo-gated. Read 15 Sep 2026.
players.free_for_workers: Yes — free profile, free applications, free courses and career content.

scan.gap:
Nothing in France, nothing regional, nothing seasonal, and — the sharpest gap — nothing anywhere that curates on staff HOUSING.

Four gaps, in order of how defensible they are.

1. FRANCE IS EMPTY. Neither curated model exists in French. Countertalk is UK-only and London-centred; Fair Job Hotels covers DE/AT/CH and stops at the German-speaking border despite already operating in Switzerland. The idea is proven in two markets and absent in the third-largest hospitality economy in Europe.

2. NOBODY CURATES ON ACCOMMODATION. Read the three criteria sets side by side — Countertalk's culture/clarity/fairness/values, the ten FAIRsprechen, and Fair Workplace Bronze/Silber/Gold — and staff accommodation appears in none of them. In alpine seasonal work, the logement is the working condition: whether there is a room, whether it is shared with three people, what is deducted for it, whether it is lost the day the contract ends. A curated alpine list that graded housing would be doing something no platform on the continent currently does, and it is the one criterion a young saisonnier can immediately verify or contradict.

3. NOBODY MEASURES CHURN. The plan says "quietly dropping those who churn staff". Countertalk reserves the right to remove an employer for "a poor or unsafe working culture" but triggers it on review, not on data. Fair Job Hotels' only ongoing instrument is the FAIRmittler — a poster in the staff area giving the number of an independent mediator, so complaints route past the employer. That mediator poster is the single most copyable mechanism in this whole lane: it is cheap, it makes the promise visible to the person who can falsify it, and it turns the workforce into the audit. But even Fair Job Hotels does not track turnover. A curated list that asked each member for its season-to-season return rate — and published the aggregate — would have the enforcement mechanism neither incumbent built.

4. NOBODY SERVES THE FIRST JOB. Hosco owns the hotel-school-to-graduate pipeline but explicitly admits any company. Countertalk is aimed at the craft/independent scene and experienced hands. Fair Job Hotels is hotel-group HR. The 17-year-old finishing a CAP and picking a first winter season is served by nobody with an opinion about the house they are walking into.
scan.bottom_line:
The thesis is NOT untested — it has been tested twice, it works, and both tests are outside France. Do not build this believing you are first; build it knowing two people already proved the demand and neither solved the hard part.

WHO ALREADY DOES THIS
Countertalk (UK, founded 2018) is the near-identical model: employers pay, candidates never do, every job is manually vetted, and the terms let them remove anyone reflecting "a poor or unsafe working culture". Fair Job Hotels e.V. (DE/AT/CH, founded 2016) is the same idea in a different wrapper: a four-stage admission judged by an expert panel on culture, young-staff development, wellbeing, pay and HR measurement, with routine rejections. Everyone else — Hosco, Caterer.com, Poached, Harri, Sirvo, OysterLink, Turijobs, Job in Tourism, HOGAPAGE — verifies that a company exists and takes its money. Hosco puts it in one sentence: "Any hospitality related company can join Hosco."

WHAT THE PRICING PROVES
Curation commands a premium. Caterer.com posts a job from £49; Countertalk charges £95 to £295 for the same act, on the same island, in the same trade — two to six times the mainstream price, because the audience has been filtered. That is the number that says employers will pay for this.

THE STRUCTURAL WARNING — AND IT IS THE IMPORTANT ONE
Countertalk after eight years has roughly a hundred employers. Curation caps supply by design, and a board with few ads has weak candidate pull. Per-advert pricing on a small curated list in a market with a three-month season is not a business — it earns for one quarter and starves for three.

Fair Job Hotels solved this and the answer is in their price list: they sell MEMBERSHIP, not advertising. €1,250 / €2,500 / €3,750 per year by headcount, recurring whether or not the house is hiring, and they rent their job listings from hotelcareer.de rather than building a board at all. Job in Tourism reaches for the same shape with its €650–€2,950 annual corporate page.

So the recommendation is structural, not cosmetic: sell an annual membership in a curated alpine list, priced by size, with visibility bought on top — not a per-ad board. Revenue then survives the off-season, and the yearly renewal is the natural moment to drop a house that churned its staff.

TWO THINGS TO STEAL, ONE TRAP TO NAME
Steal the mediator poster: Fair Job Hotels requires members to display, in the staff area, the contact details of an independent counsellor free to every employee. It converts a marketing promise into a complaint channel that routes past the employer — the cheapest enforcement instrument found in this entire lane. Steal the third-party distribution: HOGAPAGE hosts a Fair Job Hotels landing page, so the label earns reach on boards the association never had to build.

The trap: taking money from the establishments you certify is exactly the conflict Fair Job Hotels carries, and it survives only because it visibly rejects applicants. Be able to say how many houses were refused and how many were dropped. A curated list that has never turned anyone away is a directory with better copy.

scan.lane: Lane 4 — curated and values-led job platforms, any sector. Nine platforms examined, seven opened on their own sites. The lane splits into five distinct curation mechanics: (1) no curation, pay-to-appear employer branding (Welcome to the Jungle FR); (2) SILENT curation with unpublished criteria and no badge (Otta / WTTJ UK); (3) borrowed curation, where the platform never judges and defers to third-party labels (jobs_that_makesense); (4) published sector-exclusion plus a discretionary catch-all (EthicalJobs.com.au); (5) LOUD paid certification layered on an open board (Escape the City). A sixth structural twin, CoolWorks, runs his exact business model — seasonal, resort, employer-pays, candidate-free, visibility upsells — with zero curation. Prices verified by opening the operator's own page wherever the site allowed fetching; two sites (EthicalJobs main site, Escape the City app) blocked or JS-gated and are flagged.

Third-party estimates circulate (€2,000–4,500 for smaller firms, €10,000–15,000/yr for large, 1-year commitment) but these come from review-aggregator sites, NOT from WTTJ, and I am not treating them as verified.

players.size_signal: ~5.3M monthly visitors (Dec 2025, secondary source); operates FR, UK, US, ES, CZ.

It has the aesthetic of curation with none of the substance — which is precisely the credibility gap he can attack.

players.model: Curated tech job board. Companies are vetted by an internal team before being added; candidates browse a filtered universe rather than an open index.
players.price: Not published on the UK candidate site; employer pricing routes to the same sales-gated WTTJ solutions funnel. Read 2026-09-15.
players.curated: YES — AND SILENTLY. This is the single most important precedent in the lane. Companies are 'vetted by their team', but the criteria are nowhere published, there is no score, no badge, no certificate. Enforcement of employer behaviour runs through a VISIBILITY lever, not expulsion: employers are shown to more candidates if they publish transparent salaries on all jobs and respond to all applications within two weeks.
players.legal_structure: Job board (acquired by Welcome to the Jungle, Jan 2024).

players.weakness: The vetting criterion is 'exciting, innovative, fast-moving' — a quality-and-prestige filter, not a working-conditions filter. Nobody is checked on how they treat staff. It proves the silent model works commercially without proving it works ethically.

players.model: Purpose-driven job board with a paid certification layer on top: 'Top 1% Employer: Escape Certified', launched January 2025 with a 14-organisation founding cohort.

The certification audits five areas: Mission & Strategy, Leadership & Management, People Foundations, Enabling Teams, Reward & Recognition. Crucially it incorporates anonymous employee feedback, and assesses parental leave and closing salary gaps — i.e. it tests the employer's actual treatment of staff, not just its sector.
players.legal_structure: Job board + certification body + consulting arm ('Shift', people and culture consulting) + paid career-change courses.
players.free_for_workers: Yes — job search free; they separately sell career-change programmes to individuals.
players.size_signal: 14 organisations in the founding certified cohort (Jan 2025); board itself carries thousands of roles.
players.weakness: The badge model forces them to say out loud that certified employers are better, which is the exposed position he wants to avoid. Also the audit is a consulting product sold to willing employers — self-selecting, so it certifies the already-good rather than filtering out the bad. The board underneath remains largely open.

players.name: jobs_that_makesense
players.model: Impact job board run by the makesense association. Free tier plus paid Pro / Pro+ visibility tiers.
players.price: Free tier verified on their own recruiter page: 'Post up to 3 ads simultaneously for free.' Paid Pro/Pro+ prices are NOT published — the page routes to 'Contactez-nous'. Their CGU document one number: Premium Freelance service at €199/year (Article 4). Secondary sources cite €25/month or €250/year for Pro — unverified. Read 2026-09-15.

Curation is outsourced entirely to third-party labels and networks: B Corp, LUCIE 26000, Great Place to Work, Impact France, Shift Your Job, Licoornes, ESUS accreditation, plus incubators (Antropia, Ticket For Change). This is the cheapest possible way to defend a refusal: the answer to 'why not me?' is 'go get the label'.
players.legal_structure: Job board operated by an association; itself ESUS-accredited and a 'société à mission' with salary caps, employee participation in governance and dividend limits.
players.size_signal: 10,000+ impact job offers; 5,000+ recruiters; ~100,000 unique visitors/month.
players.weakness: Filters on what the organisation DOES (its mission), never on how it TREATS people. A charity that burns through staff passes; a well-run brasserie could never qualify. Useless as a conditions filter — but the borrowed-judgment trick is directly stealable.
players.source_quote: 'Post up to 3 ads simultaneously for free.' And on partners: 'jobs_that_makesense offers you the beginning of a solution with a selection of offers made by recognized incubators or networks.'

players.model: Paid-per-ad ethical job board with a published exclusion list and a discretionary withdrawal right.

players.model: Seasonal and resort job board — national parks, ski resorts, camps, ranches, beaches. Pay-per-ad plus employer-profile subscriptions and visibility boosts. THIS IS HIS BUSINESS MODEL, ALREADY BUILT, MINUS THE CURATION.

CoolWorks proves the economics work — seasonal employers will pay $149–$289 per listing or profile in exactly the resort-town context he is targeting — and proves nobody has added the filter. It is either his data supplier or his competitor: it is building the exact conditions signal he would need to curate on, in French seasonal hospitality — including alpine resorts — and it has no revenue model. It also carries the legal exposure he is trying to avoid: it publishes negative judgments about named establishments. scan.gap:
THE GAP IS REAL AND SPECIFIC. Nobody combines all four of: employer-pays / candidate-free, curation on WORKING CONDITIONS rather than sector or mission, hospitality, and local density. Each competitor holds three of the four at most. CoolWorks holds the exact commercial structure — seasonal resort employers paying $149 an ad and up to $289 a month for a profile, candidates free — with no filter whatsoever. 4dayweek.io holds a conditions filter but reduces it to one self-declared binary. Escape the City holds a genuine conditions audit (anonymous employee feedback, parental leave, pay gaps) but sells it as a loud badge to purpose-sector employers who volunteer for it. Staff-Advisor holds the French alpine-seasonal conditions data and has no money in it. Makesense refuses to make the judgment at all.

TWO ANSWERS HE ASKED FOR.

(a) YES, THE SILENT STANDARD EXISTS AND IT IS THE DOMINANT ONE IN THIS LANE. Otta / Welcome to the Jungle UK vets every company through an internal team, publishes no criteria, issues no badge and assigns no score. It communicates the value by selling the ABSENCE rather than asserting the virtue: 'Only the most exciting, innovative and fast-moving companies.' The claim is made about the collection, never about any individual employer — which is exactly what keeps it out of court. Makesense runs the second silent variant: it never judges anyone, it borrows B Corp, ESUS, LUCIE and Great Place to Work, so 'why was I refused?' is answered with 'go get the label'. The transferable mechanism from Otta is not the silence but the ENFORCEMENT LEVER: employers who publish transparent salaries and answer every application within two weeks are shown to more candidates. Behaviour is policed through ranking, not expulsion. That is the design he should copy — it produces the same filtering pressure without ever requiring him to throw a paying client off the site.

(b) NO CURATED JOB BOARD HAS BEEN SUED FOR REFUSING TO LIST AN EMPLOYER, and the reason matters. The litigation in France sits one square over, on employer-RATING sites — the ones that publish a negative judgment. On 7 May 2025 the Paris Court of Appeal (n° 23/18809) rejected a company's claim against Glassdoor for refusing to take down an anonymous ex-employee review, holding that a confidentiality clause cannot exclude current or former employees' freedom of expression about the company. Earlier, notetonentreprise.fr — a French employer-rating site carrying twelve criteria including pay, respect and management — moved to the United States under legal pressure from rated companies and then disappeared. The asymmetry is the whole finding: PUBLISHING a bad verdict draws fire; DECLINING TO PUBLISH does not. Silence is not merely more elegant than a badge, it is the legally defensible half of the pair.

THE FRENCH LEGAL FRAME FOR HIS SPECIFIC DESIGN — and it contains one genuine trap. Refusing to ADMIT an establishment is free: refus de vente between professionals was decriminalised in 1986 and abolished outright by the loi Galland of 1 July 1996. He owes no reason to anyone he declines. But DROPPING a paying establishment is not free. Article L.442-1 II du code de commerce sanctions the rupture brutale d'une relation commerciale établie and requires written notice proportionate to the relationship's duration; decisively, PARTIAL rupture counts — déréférencement, a significant cut in visibility, or a substantial change in commercial terms all qualify. 'Quietly dropping those that churn staff' is therefore the single riskiest sentence in his plan, and it is risky precisely BECAUSE they pay him. The fix is structural and costs nothing if done at the start: sell fixed-term listings and exercise NON-RENEWAL at term rather than expulsion mid-term, and write the visibility lever into the CGV from day one so a demotion is the contract operating as published rather than a partial rupture. That turns both of his enforcement actions into things he already agreed to do, in writing, before the money changed hands.
scan.bottom_line:
The model is proven and the gap is real. CoolWorks already runs his exact business — seasonal resort employers paying $149 per ad and $119–289 a month for a profile, candidates free, no placement fee — and screens nobody; Otta already proves silent curation sells, vetting every company with unpublished criteria and no badge. Nobody has put the two together in hospitality.

Three things to take from the lane. First, run the standard silently and make the quality claim about the COLLECTION, never about a named house — that is how Otta says it without saying it, and it is the half of the model that stays out of court. Second, copy Otta's enforcement lever rather than Escape the City's badge: police conditions through ranking (more visibility for houses that publish pay and answer candidates) instead of through expulsion. Third, and this is the one that will bite if ignored: under article L.442-1 II, quietly dropping a PAYING establishment is a rupture brutale d'une relation commerciale établie, and cutting its visibility counts as a partial rupture. Refusing to admit anyone is entirely free in French law since 1996; removing someone who pays you is not. Sell fixed terms, decline to renew, and write the visibility rule into the CGV before the first euro arrives.

Two flags on sourcing. Welcome to the Jungle publishes no prices at all — pure sales gate — so any figure he has been quoted for it came from a review aggregator, not from them. Escape the City's and 4dayweek.io's pricing pages would not open, so their numbers are unverified here; do not plan against them. Finally, look hard at Staff-Advisor: a French site is already collecting verified seasonal-worker reviews of hospitality establishments on accueil, organisation, ambiance and logement, with no revenue model. It is either his data supplier or the competitor that gets there first.
